summary: Aquacast Trend Detective extends the existing Aquacast ocean-intelligence platform into a NASA Earth System trend-analysis tool for the Space Apps 2026 "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!" challenge. Users select an Earth science variable (sea-surface temperature via NOAA ERDDAP, or air temperature/precipitation/wind/humidity via Meteomatics Weather API), define a region or point and time period, and the system fetches the data, runs statistical trend analysis (linear regression t-test, Mann-Kendall non-parametric test, and Sen's slope robust estimator), and reports whether the trend is significant (α=0.05). Results are visualized as a time-series chart with trend line, a study-region map on Leaflet, and a plain-language "detective summary." Reports are archived to AWS S3. Built entirely on free, open-source tools (Python/numpy, FastAPI, React, Vite, Leaflet, recharts) with no paid APIs demonstrating how students and researchers can investigate Earth system change using openly available NASA and weather data
details:
What it does: Fetches Earth science variables (NASA SST via ERDDAP; temperature/precipitation/wind/humidity via Meteomatics Weather API) for a user-defined region or point and time range, aggregates to a daily time series, and runs trend + significance analysis (linear t-test, Mann-Kendall, Sen's slope). Displays verdict, rate of change, confidence, time-series chart, and map.

Benefits: Lets students, researchers, and the public investigate whether Earth system variables are trending significantly in their region — addressing the challenge's "data detective" goal of identifying what's changing, where, how much, and whether it's statistically significant.

Intended impact: Free, no-credit-card tool for trend investigation in data-sparse regions (e.g., Gulf of Guinea / Nigerian waters), using only openly available data.

Tools: Python 3, numpy, FastAPI, React, Vite, Leaflet, recharts, axios; data from NOAA ERDDAP (NASA) and Meteomatics Weather API; AWS S3 for archiving.

Creativity: Repurposes an existing fishery heatmap pipeline into a general Earth system trend detective — same S3 archiving and ERDDAP data pattern, new statistical domain.
dataRefs: NOAA ERDDAP — NASA JPL MUR SST (sea surface temperature)
projectRefs: Meteomatics Weather API (Space Apps 2026 Global Offer)
